content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I need help with a project involving three distributed water tanks, each located approximately 3 km from the supply pumps. I'm attempting to set up wireless communication between three slave [product_name] modules and one master unit near the pumps, which should receive water level signals from the tanks. I've already programmed the network across the four [product_name] modules, but when assigning network inputs (NI) and outputs (NQ), the numbering unexpectedly skipped from NI11 to NI13; NI12 was missing. Additionally, when attempting to download the program to the [product_name] module, I received a message stating that some blocks have no connection to output, even after rewriting the program.

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. Please avoid posting about the same issue multiple times; it helps keep discussions organized. You also posted in another thread: [url]. Could you upload your programs for review? Only sharing a screenshot of the error message is not sufficient for troubleshooting.

It is likely that NI12 exists somewhere in your diagram, possibly outside the visible area. Search for it and remove any unused NI12 blocks. In previous cases, issues have occurred when NIx and NQx are not numbered sequentially. It's best to use consecutive numbering such as NI1, NI2, NI3, etc., to prevent unexpected behavior.

analysis.insight_summary: Users working with [product_name] modules experienced confusion and difficulty during network setup, specifically relating to missing or incorrectly numbered network input elements. Inconsistent interface responses and unclear error messages regarding unused blocks complicated standard programming tasks, indicating areas where product workflows or feedback could be clearer.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward network programming with consistent input/output numbering and precise, understandable error messages to facilitate troubleshooting and quick resolution of setup issues.
